events.headline: Lamar Jackson (high ankle) full again Thursday, on track for Week 8 at Buffalo; Friday designation still to come
events.detail: Jackson was a full participant Thursday per The Athletic's Jeff Zrebiec, his second straight uncapped session to open Week 8 prep. He has not played since spraining his left ankle in Week 4; Tyler Huntley started the last three games. Ian Rapoport reported Tuesday he is expected to play Sunday at Buffalo. Not cleared yet: Friday's report decides whether he carries a designation.
events.so_what: Two full practices make this as close to a fact as a forecast gets. His rushing is the premium this format pays a QB for, so he goes back in lineups unless Friday says otherwise; the fallback QB only needs to survive through Friday.

source.label: RotoWire: Lamar Jackson logs another full practice (Oct. 29)

events.headline: DJ Moore (shoulder) limited again Thursday in a non-contact jersey; Week 8 vs. Baltimore still open
events.detail: Moore was officially limited Wednesday and Thursday, wearing a non-contact jersey both days, after missing the last two games before the Bills' Week 7 bye with a recurring AC joint sprain. He followed the same pattern before Week 6, drew a Questionable tag and was ruled out on game day. Keon Coleman has filled the role in his absence and would keep it Sunday if Moore sits or is limited.
events.so_what: Still non-contact by Thursday is the same script that ended in a game-day scratch two weeks ago. Leave him on the bench unless Friday shows contact work; Coleman is the Bills receiver who gains if he sits.

source.label: RotoWire: DJ Moore officially limited Thursday (Oct. 29)

events.headline: Aaron Jones (knee) returns to practice Thursday; Jordan Mason still expected to lead the Vikings at Detroit
events.detail: Jones took part in Thursday's practice per ESPN's Kevin Seifert after sitting Wednesday. He has played through an MCL sprain since Week 2 and aggravated it in the Week 7 win over Indianapolis; imaging showed nothing significant. Jordan Mason out-snapped him 38 to 15 in Week 7, his first game off IR, with 15 carries for 68 yards. If Jones plays Sunday, expect the carries to be shared.
events.so_what: Practicing makes Jones likelier to play, not likelier to lead. Mason had the bigger role before the knee flared, so he is still the Vikings back to start; Jones is a FLEX-depth hold at best on a split.

source.label: RotoWire: Aaron Jones returns to practice Thursday (Oct. 29)

events.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs (shoulder) a full participant Thursday after a Wednesday DNP; Friday designation still to come
events.detail: Gibbs was a full participant Thursday per Detroit Sports Nation, after sitting Wednesday with a shoulder listing on a day the Lions rested several veterans. He ran 29 times for 116 yards and caught five passes in the win over Green Bay, then said he had aggravated his ankle on the final play; Dan Campbell said he "should be good." Detroit hosts Minnesota on Nov. 1.
events.so_what: A full Thursday is the signal that mattered; a bell cow coming off 34 touches stays in the lineup. Only an unexpected Friday designation changes that.

source.label: Detroit Sports Nation: Lions injury report, Oct. 29

events.headline: Jaylen Waddle (chest) spotted at Thursday practice after a Wednesday DNP; Week 8 vs. Kansas City still undecided
events.detail: Waddle was present for the media-access portion of Thursday's practice per the Denver Gazette's Chris Tomasson. He was also seen Wednesday yet listed as a non-participant, so his official Thursday level matters more than the sighting. He aggravated a chest injury on a hit in the Week 7 win at Arizona that Sean Payton called "awful"; 9News' Mike Klis expects a Questionable tag. Marvin Mims Jr. (ankle) was limited Wednesday.
events.so_what: Being seen is not participating; it also was not on Wednesday. Wait on the Friday report before starting him. If he sits, Courtland Sutton is the Broncos receiver to start and Troy Franklin picks up the snaps.

source.label: RotoWire: Jaylen Waddle spotted at Thursday's practice (Oct. 29)

events.headline: Breece Hall (quad) limited again Thursday; needs a full Friday to avoid a designation vs. Las Vegas
events.detail: Hall was limited Thursday after a limited Wednesday. He has not played since Week 3 and was inactive in Week 7 after a DNP Wednesday and two limited sessions. Aaron Glenn has said Hall is the starter when healthy; Braelon Allen, managing an ankle issue of his own, led the backfield in his absence.
events.so_what: Two limited days is one better than last week, but last week ended inactive. Only a full practice Friday makes him a start, and even then expect him to share early work with Allen.

source.label: RotoWire: Breece Hall logs another limited practice (Oct. 29)

events.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring, back) not spotted at Thursday practice; trending toward missing Sunday night vs. Washington
events.detail: Barkley was not seen warming up Thursday per The Athletic's Brooks Kubena, after a non-participant listing for Wednesday's walkthrough. He hurt his back on a 29-yard run in Monday's 38-21 loss to Dallas, his first game back from a two-game absence, and played only nine snaps. Dameon Pierce went to IR. Jaydon Blue, promoted from the practice squad, is the top healthy alternative, and Elijah Mitchell may be elevated before Sunday night's game against Washington.
events.so_what: Plan as if he sits. A Sunday night kickoff leaves no late pivot if he is ruled out at inactives, so set a Sunday afternoon replacement now. Neither Blue nor Mitchell is a trusted start on an unknown split.

source.label: RotoWire: Saquon Barkley not spotted at practice (Oct. 29)

events.headline: A.J. Brown (ankle, knee) a non-participant Thursday; aggravated knee puts Week 8 vs. Miami in doubt
events.detail: The Patriots listed Brown as a non-participant Thursday after a limited Wednesday, matching Ian Rapoport's report that a recently aggravated knee has his status for Sunday against Miami in doubt. Brown has six catches for 75 yards on 16 targets in two games since returning from a four-game ankle absence.
events.so_what: Trending the wrong way, and the production since his return was thin even when healthy. Line up a replacement now and treat Friday as the deciding report.

source.label: RotoWire: A.J. Brown confirmed as non-participant Thursday (Oct. 29)

events.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ankle) a full participant Thursday after a planned Wednesday rest
events.detail: St. Brown sat Wednesday as planned and was a full participant Thursday per Detroit Sports Nation. Kerby Joseph and Ennis Rakestraw Jr. were limited for a second straight day. Detroit hosts Minnesota on Nov. 1.
events.so_what: The rest day played out as advertised. Treat him as a normal start unless Friday adds a designation.

source.label: Detroit Sports Nation: Lions injury report, Oct. 29

events.headline: Jaylin Noel (turf toe) placed on season-ending IR; Texans claim Emari Demercado off waivers
events.detail: Houston moved Noel to injured reserve Wednesday with the turf toe he suffered in the Week 7 overtime loss to the Giants, a move RotoWire reports as season-ending, and used the spot to claim RB Emari Demercado off waivers from Dallas for depth while David Montgomery (groin) is out. The Texans are on bye in Week 8.
events.so_what: Noel leaving the rotation concentrates the Houston targets on Nico Collins and Tank Dell coming out of the bye. Demercado is depth behind Woody Marks, not a pickup.

source.label: RotoWire: Emari Demercado claimed off waivers by Houston (Oct. 28)

events.headline: Ja'Marr Chase (ankle, rest) does not practice Wednesday
events.detail: The Bengals listed Chase as a non-participant Wednesday for a veteran rest day and an ankle injury. Cincinnati also placed TE Erick All on IR with a torn ACL.
events.so_what: A rest-and-ankle Wednesday is usually maintenance for a starter of his volume, but it is still on the report; check that he practices Thursday or Friday before treating him as a locked start.

source.label: CBS Sports: NFL Week 8 injury report (Oct. 28)

events.headline: Kenneth Gainwell (hip) misses Wednesday practice; Bucky Irving leads Tampa Bay into Atlanta
events.detail: Gainwell did not practice Wednesday with the hip injury that sent him briefly to the sideline in Week 7, when he still finished with 14 carries for 88 yards in a 49-rush game. Bucky Irving remains the lead back and Sean Tucker is the next man up. Emeka Egbuka (concussion, foot) was limited and Baker Mayfield (thumb) was full.
events.so_what: Gainwell's Week 7 volume came from a lopsided script, so he is a handcuff rather than a start either way. If he sits, Tucker picks up the change-of-pace snaps and Irving's share grows.

source.label: NFL.com: news roundup, Wednesday Oct. 28

events.headline: Commanders put Terry McLaurin on IR, out for the season with a torn patellar tendon; Stefon Diggs DNP Wednesday
events.detail: Washington formally placed McLaurin on injured reserve Wednesday after an MRI confirmed the torn patellar tendon from Week 6 against San Francisco; he had 15 catches for 230 yards and a TD in four games. Van Jefferson was promoted from the practice squad. Stefon Diggs (hand, hamstring, rest) did not practice and Treylon Burks (foot) was limited. Jayden Daniels (elbow) was full.
events.so_what: McLaurin is a drop in any league without a deep IR need. Diggs is the target leader by default, but a three-reason DNP makes him a Friday-report call for Sunday night against Philadelphia.

source.label: RotoWire: Terry McLaurin heads to IR (Oct. 28)

events.headline: Davante Adams (hamstring) has a successful cleanup and could return at the sooner end of a 6-10 week timeline
events.detail: Sean McVay said Wednesday that Adams' hamstring cleanup procedure went well and he could be back on the sooner end of the six-to-ten-week window. TE Terrance Ferguson (ankle) remains on IR and will not return to practice this week, and Colby Parkinson (rib) did not practice.
events.so_what: Even the short end of that window is about six weeks, so Adams is an IR stash for a fantasy playoff run, not a hold on a five-man bench. Only roster him if an IR slot is open.

source.label: NFL.com: news roundup, Wednesday Oct. 28

events.headline: Josh Downs reportedly requests a trade as the Colts sell after firing GM Chris Ballard
events.detail: ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported that Downs, in the final year of his rookie deal, has asked to be traded, and multiple teams have shown interest. Asked Wednesday, Downs said "I'm here today, but whatever comes my way comes my way." He has 26 catches for 307 yards and no TDs in seven games. Indianapolis fired Ballard this week and has already moved linemen Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner; Shane Steichen says Jonathan Taylor has not asked out. The deadline is Nov. 10.
events.so_what: Nothing changes until he is moved. A trade to a team that uses him in the slot full time could raise his target floor, while staying in a selling offense caps it; he is a bench hold, not a start, while it plays out.

source.label: CBS Sports: Josh Downs landing spots after Colts WR reportedly asks out (Oct. 28)

events.headline: Matthew Golden (shoulder, foot) Questionable for Thursday vs. Carolina after a limited Wednesday walkthrough
events.detail: Golden sat out Monday and Tuesday, then was limited in Wednesday's walkthrough and carries a Questionable tag into Thursday night's home game against Carolina. The foot issue is new this week on top of the shoulder from last week's report; he played 85% of the snaps through both at Detroit in Week 7. Devonte Wyatt is also Questionable. Final word comes with inactives about 90 minutes before the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff. Jayden Reed and Skyy Moore remain on IR, so Green Bay's receiver depth is thin.
events.so_what: A Questionable tag on a Thursday game is the worst kind: if he sits you find out about 90 minutes before kickoff with only Sunday players left to swap in. Start him only if your bench has a comparable Sunday or Monday option you can slot in after inactives post; otherwise take the safer play.

source.label: NBC Sports (PFT): Matthew Golden, Devonte Wyatt questionable for Thursday night (Oct. 28)

events.headline: Ladd McConkey (concussion) a full participant Wednesday; Tre' Harris (hamstring) limited
events.detail: McConkey was listed as a full participant Wednesday after practicing Monday in a non-contact jersey while in the concussion protocol; he missed Week 6 with a foot injury before the concussion. Tre' Harris (hamstring) was limited, and Brenen Thompson (quad, hamstring) did not practice. Omarion Hampton played 49% of the snaps in a three-back rotation with Kimani Vidal in Week 6.
events.so_what: A full practice is a strong sign he has cleared contact, but the protocol still ends with an independent neurologist, so he is not a fact until he carries no designation. Hampton's 49% snap share in a rotation keeps him a FLEX at best until the backfield sorts out.

source.label: NFL.com: news roundup, Wednesday Oct. 28

events.headline: Tyrone Tracy (hamstring) headed to IR, out through at least Week 12; Cam Skattebo expects to be fine after his 124-yard day
events.detail: Giants GM Joe Schoen said Tuesday that Tyrone Tracy Jr. will be placed on injured reserve with the hamstring he hurt in Sunday's overtime win over Houston. It is not season-ending, but IR costs him at least the next four games. Devin Singletary is expected to be the top complement to Skattebo, and the Giants plan to sign Greg Desrosiers off the Chargers' practice squad for depth. Skattebo, back in the lead role after Najee Harris' Oct. 20 release, carried 17 times for 124 yards and a TD, felt something in his own hamstring on a 42-yard overtime run, and told ESPN on Monday he believes he will be fine; there is still no team diagnosis. The Giants are on bye in Week 8.
events.so_what: Skattebo earned the job back on volume and efficiency, so he is a starter-level back once the bye passes, provided his own hamstring checks out. With Tracy on IR, Singletary is the clear second back and the only Giant worth a bench spot as Skattebo insurance. Nobody needs to start a Giant in Week 8.

source.label: RotoWire: Tyrone Tracy bound for IR (Oct. 27)

events.headline: Rashid Shaheed (knee) avoids the worst case, Mike Macdonald says early word is 'positive'; no timeline for Monday vs. Chicago
events.detail: Shaheed left Seattle's 20-3 win over Kansas City after 22 snaps (two catches on three targets for one yard) following a collision with Jaxon Smith-Njigba. On Monday Mike Macdonald said the early word on the knee is "positive," but gave no timeline. Shaheed had a full left meniscus repair in 2024 that cost him 11 games. LT Charles Cross has a high ankle sprain, with a hoped-for return in one to two weeks. Seattle hosts Chicago next Monday night, which buys an extra day.
events.so_what: Better than feared, but still not a start until he practices. With a Monday kickoff, any lineup holding him needs a fallback that plays earlier in the week.

source.label: RotoWire: Rashid Shaheed avoids worst-case knee issue (Oct. 26)

events.headline: Christian McCaffrey has a mild hamstring strain, Kyle Shanahan "pretty optimistic" for Week 9 after the bye
events.detail: McCaffrey scored on San Francisco's opening drive at Atlanta, sat the second quarter, then returned and finished with 7 carries for 39 yards and a TD plus 6 catches for 61 in the 29-20 loss; Kaelon Black ran for 63 yards and a TD while he was out. On Monday Shanahan called it a mild hamstring strain and said the 49ers are "pretty optimistic" he plays after the Week 8 bye, against Las Vegas.
events.so_what: No lineup decision until Week 9 because of the bye. A mild strain with two weeks to heal is a hold, not a sell. Black is a handcuff, not a start.

source.label: Heavy: Shanahan gives injury timeline update on McCaffrey (Oct. 26)

events.headline: Zach Charbonnet to practice fully with a chance to debut Monday vs. Chicago; Jadarian Price designated to return from IR
events.detail: Charbonnet sat Week 7 after his activation from PUP (torn ACL) and will practice fully this week. Price, a rookie who missed four games on IR with a chest injury, is eligible and will practice. Mike Macdonald would not commit: "Could they both play? Yes. Could neither play? Yes." Emanuel Wilson has been carrying the lead role, and Velus Jones Jr. has a hamstring injury of unknown severity.
events.so_what: Both are forecasts, and the Monday-night kickoff means you will know the inactives only after the rest of your lineup locks. Do not start Charbonnet or Price blind this week. Wilson stays a FLEX until one of them is active, and loses value fast once they are.

source.label: Seahawks.com: This week's plan for Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet (Oct. 26)

events.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) set to practice Wednesday after missing two games; Week 8 at Dallas still open
events.detail: Mike LaFleur said Monday that Love is expected to practice Wednesday, per The Arizona Republic's Theo Mackie and the team site's Darren Urban. Love has missed Weeks 6 and 7 with a lingering ankle issue, and Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight split the backfield in his absence. Arizona plays at Dallas on Sunday, and he will likely need several straight practices to get there.
events.so_what: A Wednesday practice is a start, not a clearance; Love likely needs a couple of sessions before he gets a designation, so hold him and check Friday. If he plays, expect a share rather than his early-season workload, which leaves Allgeier and Knight as FLEX-only and the touchdown upside split.

source.label: NBC Sports: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) to practice Wednesday (Oct. 26)

events.headline: Tony Pollard runs 25 times for 129 yards and three TDs with Tyjae Spears inactive in a 27-24 loss to Cleveland
events.detail: With Spears (knee) and Nicholas Singleton inactive, Pollard carried the Tennessee backfield: 25 carries, 129 yards, three rushing TDs, plus three catches for 26 yards, per FantasyPros and PFF. Tennessee rushed for 141 yards as a team. He had scored two touchdowns in his previous 10 games combined. Calvin Ridley (hip) was also inactive, and Elic Ayomanor took his snaps. Spears (knee) did not practice Wednesday to open Week 8.
events.so_what: While Spears is out Pollard is the whole Titans run game, which makes him an RB2 with touchdown upside. Spears missing Wednesday points to another week of that volume; a practice by Friday would cut it back to a split.

source.label: FantasyPros: Tony Pollard scores three TDs in Week 7 (Oct. 25)

events.headline: Woody Marks plays 89% of the snaps with David Montgomery (groin) out; Jaylin Noel leaves with a toe injury in a walking boot
events.detail: With Montgomery out a second straight week, Marks took 89% of Houston's snaps and ran 19 times for 66 yards in the overtime loss to the Giants. WR Jaylin Noel left with a turf toe injury, DeMeco Ryans said, and was in a walking boot afterward. Tank Dell played his first game since his 2024 knee injury as Houston used six receivers; Nico Collins ran a route on 80% or more of dropbacks but has drawn five targets in each of his last two games. Houston is on bye in Week 8. By Tuesday Noel's turf toe was still being evaluated, with the severity unclear.
events.so_what: Marks is a volume RB2 for as long as Montgomery sits; Montgomery is a bench hold, not a drop. Noel's injury trims the receiver rotation, which helps Collins' target count more than anyone else.

source.label: PFF: NFL Week 7 recap, immediate fantasy takeaways (Oct. 25)

events.headline: Jonah Coleman leads the Broncos backfield in his first game off IR: 50% of the snaps, 9 carries for 54 yards
events.detail: Coleman, activated from IR the day before, out-snapped RJ Harvey (25%) and J.K. Dobbins (21%) in the 30-16 win over Arizona, adding two catches for 15 yards. Dobbins (6 carries, 1-yard TD) declined interviews afterward; Harvey turned three carries and two targets into 60 yards and a TD. Coleman was the only Denver back without a touchdown. Denver hosts Kansas City in Week 8.
events.so_what: A three-way split with the rookie on top is a start for nobody yet, but Coleman holds the early-down role that matters most here. Treat him as a FLEX-depth add and Dobbins as the one losing value; goal-line work is still unsettled.

source.label: NBC Sports: Coleman operates as Broncos lead back in Week 7 (Oct. 25)
